claims.claim_ar: تكرار حرف الباء في «فَبِظُلْمٍ ... وَبِصَدِّهِمْ» تكثيف لسببَي التحريم والنتيجة، ويقوّي رابط السببية.
claims.claim_en: Repetition of the preposition bi- in 'fa-bi-dhulmin ... wa-bi-saddihim' intensifies the causal link and emphasizes the reasons leading to the prohibition.
claims.needs_review_reason: Interpretive claim based on exegetical phrasing; the verse shows two bi- phrases but the emphatic function is inferred from style rather than explicit grammar.
claims.rhetorical_effect: strengthens perceived causality and cohesion between the two reasons given for the divine action

claims.source_quote_ar: ما حرمنا عليهم الطيبات إلا لظلم عظيم
claims.claim_ar: تضاد بين الحكمين «حَرَّمْنَا ... الطيبات» و«أُحِلَّتْ لَهُمْ» في الإسناد التفسيري يبرز تبدّل الحكم والسياسة الإلهية بسبب ظلمهم.
claims.claim_en: A contrast (tibaq) between 'We made unlawful ... good things' and the prior state of those things being lawful highlights a reversal of legal status as a result of their wrongdoing.
claims.rhetorical_effect: foregrounds moral causation: wrongdoing produces legal and moral consequences

claims.source_quote_ar: ما حرمنا عليهم الطيبات إلا لظلم عظيم ارتكبوه
claims.claim_ar: السياق التفسيري يستخدم أداة الاستثناء «إلا» لحصر سبب التحريم في «ظلم عظيم»، أي تقييد الحكم بشرط واحد مُبيّن.
claims.claim_en: The exegetical phrasing uses the exception 'illa' to confine the reason for the prohibition to a single, grave wrongdoing, thereby restricting the explanation.
claims.needs_review_reason: The explicit particle 'إلا' appears in the tafsir text rather than verbatim in the isolated verse wording; attribution relies on exegetical expansion.
claims.rhetorical_effect: narrows the interpretive cause, directing the reader to a single decisive moral reason

claims.claim_ar: تعابير مثل «صَدّهم عن سبيل الله» تُقدَّم ككناية عن الإعاقة والفساد (كالرشوة والتحريف) لا كمعنى حرفي فقط.
claims.claim_en: Phrases like 'their blocking (sadd) of the way of God' function as a kenāyah (indirect expression) for obstruction and corrupt practices (e.g., bribery, distortion), not merely a literal blocking.
claims.needs_review_reason: Relies on the exegetical gloss which supplies the specific referent (bribery, distortion); the kenāyah reading is interpretive though well-attested in tafsir.
claims.rhetorical_effect: casts the action as morally charged and concretely condemnable by using an indirect, loaded expression
